WHEREAS, Section 8(1)(e) of the Michigan Open Meetings Act, MCL 15.268(1)(e), provides that a
public body may meet in closed session to consult with its attorney regarding trial or settlement strategy
in connection with specific pending litigation where an open meeting would have a detrimental financial
effect on the litigating or settlement position of the body; and
WHEREAS, Section 8(1)(d) of the Michigan Open Meetings Act, MCL 15.268(1)(d), permits a public
body to meet in closed session to consider the purchase or lease of real property up to the time an option
to purchase or lease that property is obtained; and
                                                                                                             1


May 19, 2026, Special Meeting Draft



WHEREAS, Section 8(1)(h) of the Michigan Open Meetings Act, MCL 15.268(1)(h), permits a public
body to meet in closed session to consider material exempt from discussion or disclosure by state or
federal statue, including attorney-client privileged communications; and
WHEREAS, The City of Pontiac Law Department has requested that the City Council convene in closed
session for the following purposes:

          • To discuss litigation strategy concerning JADC Ventures, LLC et. Al. v City of Pontiac;
          • To discuss real estate strategy concerning City Property interest; and
          • To discuss and consider privileged attorney-client communications and memorandum exempt
from disclosure by law.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Pontiac City Qounpil of Pontiac hereby determines
that it is necessary to meet in closed session pursuant to Sections 8(l')(d), 8(1)(e), and 8(1)(h) of the
Michigan Open Meetings Act, MCL 15 .268(1 )( d), (e ), and (h), for .1:he:,purposes stated above.

26-110 (G)     Resolution Declaring May Motorcycle Awareness Month. Moved by Councilperson
Campbell and seconded by Councilperson Jones.



                                                                                                                                                                  4


May 19, 2026, Regular Meeting Draft Minutes



WHEREAS, the City of Pontiac is committed to promoting roadway safety for all residents, visitors, and
commuters; and
WHEREAS, motorcycles are a common and important mode of transportation, recreation, and economic
activity throughout the State of Michigan and the City of Pontiac; and
WHEREAS, motorcyclists are more vulnerable on roadways due to their smaller size and reduced
visibility compared to other vehicles; and
WHEREAS, increasing public awareness of motorcycles on roadways can reduce accidents, injuries, and
fatalities by encouraging all drivers to share the road responsibly; and
WHEREAS, Motorcycle Awareness Month provides an opportunity to remind motorists to remain
attentive, check blind spots, and give motorcycles the space and re~m:lP1Jhey deserve; and
WHEREAS, the Pontiac City Council supports efforts to impro".,e,~¥6Ji'c safety, protect motorcyclists,
and promote responsible driving behaviors within the commuµity;> (
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the PontiacCity.CQ~~H hereby declares the month of
May as Motorcycle Awareness Month in the City of Po]J.ti~biafid ',,,ltt;\)>t
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that all residents are,.ehpp,rtraged to incre~~~~their awareness of
motorcycles on the road and to practice safe drivi11ghagits to help prevent'1voi'dable accidents; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the City of P~4ti4c joins communities a~ross the nation in
promoting motorcycle safety and awareness initiative~ during the 19-qµth ofMay''and;throughout the year.

Exhibit A




                                           Ordinance No. 2495

            An Ordinance to appropriate the sums of money necessary to meet the expenditures
                   set forth in the budget recommended for the operation of the City of Pontiac,
                   Michigan; to defray the debts, expenditures, and liabilities of said City for the
                   fiscal year beginning the first day of July 2026.

            Whereas, the proposed General Appropriations Act is required to be effective July 1, 2026,
            so the City can legally operate.

            The City of Pontiac Ordains:

            Section 1. Title.

            This ordinance shall be known as the City of Pontiac 2026-2027 General Appropriations Act.

            •Section 2. Public Hearing on the Budget.

            Pursuant to MCL 141.412 and 141.413, notice of a public hearing on the proposed budget
            was published in the Oakland Press, a newspaper of general circulation April 27, 2026, and
            a public hearing on the proposed budget was held on May 5, 2026 and May 19, 2026.

            Section 3. Millage Levy, Administration Fee, and Penalties.

            The City Council for the City of Pontiac shall authorize the following millages to be levied and
            collected on the general property tax of all real and personal property within the City upon
            the current tax roll: an allocated millage of 10.8869 operating; 1.3606 capital improvement;
            2. 7215 sanitation; 0.4826 senior services; 1.4483 youth center; and an additional voted
            operating millage of 1.0841. The City Treasurer is hereby authorized to impose a one percent
            (1 %) property tax administration fee for all property taxes due, a three percent (3%) late
            penalty charge when applicable and a one percent (1 %) monthly interest charge when
            applicable in conformance with Section 44 of Public Act 206 of 1893.

            Section 4. Adoption of Budget by Function.

            The City Council of the City of Pontiac received a recommended budget on April 16, 2026,
            from Mayor Mike McGuinness. The administration has incorporated changes requested by
            City Council during various public presentations by the departments. The City Council of the
            City of Pontiac adopts the 2026-2027 fiscal year budgets for the various funds by
            department. City officials responsible for the expenditures authorized in the budget may
            expend City funds up to, but not to exceed, the total appropriation authorized for each
            department.


Section 5. Payment of Bills.

Pursuant to the Pontiac Home Rule Charter, the Michigan Uniform Budgeting and Accounting
Act (Public Act 2 of 1968, MCL 141.421 et seq.), and the Accounting Procedures Manual for
Local Governments in Michigan, all claims (bills) against the City shall be approved by the
Finance Director of the City of Pontiac prior to being paid.

Section 6. Budgeted Revenues and Expenditures

Estimated total revenues and expenditures, including transfers in and out and other sources,
for the various funds of the City of Pontiac beginning July 1, 2026, are $126.2 million in
revenues and $146.4 million in expenditures.

Section 7. Specific Appropriations.

There are no specific appropriations contained in the budget.

Section 8. Periodic Financial Reports.

The Finance Director shall provide the Mayor and City Council financial reports on a monthly
basis.

Section 9. Budget Monitoring and Amending.

Whenever it appears to the Finance Director that the actual and probable revenues in any
fund will be less than the estimated revenues upon which appropriations from such fund
were based, and when it appears that expenditures will exceed an appropriation upon which
appropriations from such fund were based, the Finance Director shall present to the Mayor
recommendations to prevent expenditures from exceeding available revenues or
appropriations for the fiscal year. Such recommendations shall include proposals for
reducing appropriations, increasing revenues or both. The Finance Director is hereby
authorized to make budget amendments within a department in amounts that do not exceed
ten thousand dollars ($10,000) within a fiscal year. Any budget amendments to a department
that exceed ten thousand dollars ($1 0,000)within a fiscal year must be approved by the City
Council prior to amendment. All transfers in and transfers out between appropriation
departments exceeding ten thousand dollars ($10,000) must be approved by City Council
prior to such transfer.

Section 1O. Severability.

If any section, clause, or provision of this Ordinance shall be declared to be unconstitutional,
void, or illegal by any Court of competent jurisdiction, such section, clause, or provision
declared to be unconstitutional, void, or illegal shall thereby cease to be a part of this
Ordinance, but the remainder of this Ordinance shall stand and be in full force and effect.


Section 11. Repealer.

All Ordinances or parts of Ordinances in conflict herewith are hereby repealed only to the
extent necessary to give this Ordinance full force and effect.

Section 12. Publication.

The Clerk shall publish this Ordinance in a newspaper of general circulation.

Section 13. Effective Date.

This Ordinance was passed on May 19, 2026.

                  CITY OF PONTIAC RESOLUTION
                  CELEBRATING 100th MILESTONE
                   OF MS. MARY STRAWDER
Whereas, the City of Pontiac has been privileged to have many
amazing community members live in our great City and make a
positive impact for our residents; and,
Whereas, Ms. Mary Strawder has lived in our great City for
decades, and we are blessed to have her as part of the greater
Pontiac family; and,
Whereas, Ms. Strawder is turning a remarkable 100 years old on
June 20, 2026; and,
Whereas, her centennial milestone will be celebrated, which is a
profound loss for her family and for our community; now,
Therefore, Be It Resolved, the Pontiac City Council in
partnership with Mayor Mike McGuinness hereby celebrates the
100th birthday milestone of Ms. Mary Strawder; and further
Resolved, the City Council expresses our deepest gratitude for
Ms. Strawder' s years of positive impact upon our City and to our
many past and present citizens whose lives she impacted; and
further
Resolved, we wish Ms. Strawder the very best of celebrations
and we are incredibly thrilled for her and for her family.

                  PONTIAC CITY COUNCIL RESOLUTION
                              Recognizing Juneteenth
                               in the City of Pontiac
 Whereas, Juneteenth is celebrated in recognition of June 19, 1865 as the date on which
 news of the end of slavery reached the slaves in the southwestern states of the United
 States of America; and,
 Whereas, news of the end of slavery did not reach the frontier area of the United States,
 in particular the State of Texas and other southwestern states, until months after the
 conclusion of the American Civil War, more than two and a half years after President
 Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation on January 1, 1863; and,
 Whereas, on June 19, 1865, Union soldiers, led by Major General Gordon Granger,
 arrived in Galveston, Texas with news that the Civil War had ended and the enslaved
 were free; and,
, Whereas, African Americans who had been slaves in the southwest celebrated June 19,
  commonly known as Juneteenth Independence Day, as inspiration and encouragement
  for future generations, and African Americans from the southwest continued the
  tradition observing Juneteenth through the generations that followed; and,
 Whereas, Juneteenth has continued to grow in widespread familiarity and celebration
 throughout the entire country and is now a recognized federal holiday; now,
 Therefore, Be It Resolved, the City Council, in partnership with Mayor McGuinness,
 hereby recognizes June 19, 2026 as Juneteenth in the City of Pontiac; and further
 Resolved, the City Council warmly welcomes the many programs and observances that
 are being planned in the City of Pontiac to mark Juneteenth this year; and further
 Resolved, the City of Pontiac supports the continued celebration of Juneteenth to
 provide an opportunity for the people of Pontiac and the United States to learn more
 about the past and to better understand this important, dark era in history.

                PONTIAC CITY COUNCIL RESOLUTION
                 Recognizing June as LGBTQIA+
                Pride Month in the City of Pontiac
Whereas, the City of Pontiac strives to be an exceptional place for all of our residents to
live, work, enjoy, learn, and thrive and we accept and welcome all people of diverse
backgrounds and believes a diverse population leads to a more vibrant community; and,
Whereas, the Pontiac community benefits from fostering greater acceptance of all
residents and further preventing discrimination, harassment, and bullying based on
sexual orientation, gender identity, and gender expression; and,
Whereas, it is imperative that people of all ages in our community, regardless of sexual
orientation, gender identity, and gender expression, feel valued, safe, and supported by
their peers and community leaders; and,
Whereas, Pontiac's lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans gender, queer, intersex, asexual, and
nonbinary identifying (LGBTQIA+) community members are a vital part of our overall
community and contribute to making our City stronger and more inclusive; and,
Whereas, LGBTQIA + Pride Month is celebrated nationally each June, with origins in the
June 1969 New York City uprising at the Stonewall Inn; now,
Therefore, Be It Resolved, the Pontiac City Council, in partnership with Mayor Mike
McGuinness, hereby recognizes June as LGBTQIA + Pride Month in Pontiac; and further
Resolved, the City Council affirms that Pontiac lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender,
queer, intersex, asexual, and nonbinary identifying residents are accepted, welcomed,
and valued members of our Pontiac community; and further
Resolved, the City of Pontiac renews our commitment to fostering greater acceptance,
safety, and inclusion of residents in our community regardless of sexual orientation,
sexuality, gender identity, and gender expression.

                PONTIAC CITY COUNCIL RESOLUTION
                Recognizing June as Men's Health
                  Month in the City of Pontiac
Whereas, the City of Pontiac strives to be an exceptional place for all of our residents to
live, work, enjoy, and thrive; and,
Whereas, despite advances in medical technology and research, presently in America
men continue to live an average of five years less than women, with Native American
and African American men having the lowest life expectancy; and,
Whereas, educating the public and health care providers about the importance of a
healthy lifestyle and early detection of male health problems will result in reducing rates
of mortality from disease, as well as improve male residents' quality of life; and,
Whereas, men who are educated about the value that preventive health can play in
prolonging their lifespan and their role as family members will be more likely to
participate in health screenings and other preventive health practices; and,
Whereas, Father's Day falls in June, and fathers who maintain a healthy lifestyle are role
models for their children and will inevitably help raise happier, healthier children; now,
Therefore, Be It Resolved, the Pontiac City Council, in partnership with Mayor Mike
McGuinness, hereby recognizes June as Men's Health Month in Pontiac; and further
Resolved, the City Council encourages residents to strengthen their awareness and
understanding of the importance of a healthy lifestyle, regular exercise, health
screenings, and regular medical check-ups; and further
Resolved, we are hopeful that Men's Health Month draws greater attention to the
positive health attitudes and preventive health practices for men, boys, and their
families, and motivate families to lessen the pervasive health challenges of heart disease,
mental health challenges, diabetes, and prostate, testicular, and colon cancer.

                 CITY OF PONTIAC RESOLUTION
                   Recognizing the 100th Anniversary
                 Milestone of Pontiac Motor Division &
                 Welcoming the Pontiac-Oakland Club
                  International Convention to Pontiac
Whereas, the Pontiac vehicle brand was introduced by the Oakland Motor Car
Division of General Motors, which was based in our City of Pontiac, in January
1926 and was a roaring success, selling over 76,000 vehicles in their first year; and,

Whereas, the massive success of the Pontiac brand birthed the renamed Pontiac
Motor Division of General Motors, which was headquartered in our City of
Pontiac for seventy years, and was a major driver of our City's growth; and,
Whereas, for generations the iconic Pontiac automobiles that became synonymous
with our historic City of Pontiac helped shape American culture, manufactured
millions of vehicles, helped win World War II for America with epic wartime
production, generated great wealth for our citizens, our city, our county, our
region, our state, and our nation; and,
Whereas, the iconic Pontiac brand is turning 100 years old this year, the City of
Pontiac has partnered with Pontiac Transportation Museum for many celebratory
activities, and the Pontiac-Oakland Club International is holding their Annual
Convention in the City of Pontiac in June 2026; now,
Therefore, Be It Resolved, the Pontiac City Council and Pontiac Mayor Mike
McGuinness hereby celebrates the phenomenal milestone of Pontiac Motor
Division's 100th anniversary; and further
Resolved, the City hereby welcomes Pontiac-Oakland Club International and their
guests to the City of Pontiac for their Annual Convention; and further
Resolved, the City Council acknowledges the remarkable, rich, and enduring
legacy of the products and people that defined the Pontiac Motor Division and
made an indelible, defining mark on our City's history.

                                   ARTICLES. OF INCORPORATION
                                                            OF
                           CATHOLIC COMMUNITY RESPONSE TEAM
                               (a Michigan Nonprofit Corporation)
       Pursuant to the provisions of Act 162, Public Acts of 1982, as amended (the "Act"), the
undersigned Corporation executes the following Articles:

                                                      ARTICLE I

        The name of the Corporation is CATHOLIC COMMUNITY RESPONSE TEAM.

                                                     ARTICLE II

        The Corporation is organized exclusively for charitable, educational and scientific
purposes as described in Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code (the "Code"), providing
direct support and referral services to those in need in the areas of mental health, homelessness,
housing, basic needs, identification documentation, transportation and similar services and
conducting all activities incidental or necessary to accomplishing the foregoing purposes or
otherwise permitted by Section 501(c)(3) of the Code.

                                                     ARTICLE III

       The Corporation will at all times be conducted as an organization descdbed in Section
50l(c)(3) of the Code. The Corporation will not canyon any activities which are not permitted
to be carried on by (a) a corporation exempt from federal income tax under Section 501(c)(3) of
the Code, (b) a corporation eligible to receive tax deductible contributions under Section 170(c)
and Section 2055, Section 2522 or Section 2106 of the Code, or (c) a nonprofit corporation
organized under the laws of the State of Michigan pursuant to the Act.

        No part ofth~ assets or net earnings of the Corporation may inure to the benefit of or be
distributable to its Directors, officers, or other private persons; provided, however, that the


ClarkHill\L0917\440804\267951417.v 1-7/19/22


Corporation is authorized and empowered to pay reasonable compensation for services rendered
and to make payments and distributions in furtherance of its charitable purposes.

        No substantial part of the activities of the Corporation will be the carrying on of
propaganda or otherwise attempting to influence legislation. The Corporation will not participate
or intervene in any political campaign on behalf of or in opposition to any candidate for public
office and will not publish or distribute statements relating to political campaigns.

                                              ARTICLE IV

         The Corporation is organized on a nonstock basis.

         The Corporation has no real property or personal property assets.

         The Corporation is to be financed through contributions and investment income.

         The Corporation is organized on a directorship basis.

                                              ARTICLEV

         The name of the resident agent at the registered office is Barbara Williams.

         The address of the registered office is 132 Franklin Blvd., #203, Pontiac, MI 48309.

                                              ARTICLE VI

       The name and address of the incorporator is Maria A. Toma, 500 Woodward Ave., Suite
3500, Detroit, MI 48226.

                                              ARTICLE VII

         Except as otherwise provided by law, a Director or volunteer officer of the Corporation is
not liable to the Corporation or its members for money damages for any action taken or any
failure to take any action as a Director or volunteer officer.

        The Corporation assumes all liability to any person other than the Corporation or its
members for all acts or omissions of a volunteer Director incurred in the good faith performance
of his or her duties as a volunteer Director.

       The Corporation assumes the liability for all acts or omissions ofa volunteer officer,
provided that:

                 (a)      the volunteer was acting or reasonably believed he or she was
                          acting within the scope of his or her authority;

                 (b)      the volunteer was acting in good faith;

                 (c)      the volunteer's conduct did not amount to gross negligence or
                          willful and wanton misconduct;


ClarkHill\L0917\440804\267951417.vl-7/19/22


                 (d)      the volunteer's conduct was not an intentional tort; and

                 (e)      the volunteer's conduct was not a tort arising out of the ownership,
                          maintenance or use of a motor vehicle as described in Section
                          209(e)(v) of the Act.

                                              ARTICLE VIII

       Upon the termination, dissolution or winding up of the Corporation, the Board of
Directors will distribute all remaining assets of the Corporation for a purpose or to an
organization or organizations described in Section 501(c)(3) of the Code.

                                              ARTICLE IX

        These Articles may be amended or repealed by a majority vote of the Directors of the
Corporation then in office at any regular or special meeting of the Directors provided that any
statutory notice requirements are met.

                                                               BYLAWS

                                                                   OF
                                       CATHOLIC COMMUNITY.RESPONSE TEAM

                                                 (A Michigan Nonprofit Corporation)

                                                               ARTICLE I
                                                            Board of Directors

                   Section I.     Directorship. The Corporation is organized upon a directorship basis. Tbe
            property, business and affairs of the Corporation will be managed by its Board of Directors.

                    Section 2.    Number and Term of Office. The Board of Directors shall consist of not less
            than nine (9) nor more than fifteen (15) persons, as determined by the Board of Directors.

                     Each member of the initial Board of Directors will serve until the first amma1 meeting of
            the Corporation at which time he or she will cease to be a Director unless otherwise elected or
            appointed as provided herein. Thereafter, the term of office of any Director will commence upon
            his or her election or appointment by the affilmative vote of a majority of the Directors then in
,....._,_   office. The Director's term will continue until the next annual meeting of the Corporation and
            thereafter until his or her successor is chosen or until his or her death, resignation or removal prior
            to the nextannual meeting.

                    Section 3.     Resignation 1 Removal and Vacancies. A Director may resign by written
            notice to the Corporation. The resignation will be effective upon its receipt by the Corporation or
            a subsequent time as set forth in the notice of resignation. A Director may be removed with cause
            by the affirmative vote of amajorityofthe Directors then.in office. A Director appointed or elected
            by a person or persons other than the Board of Directors of the Corporation may be removed with
            or without cause by the person or persons that appointed or elected that Director.

                    If avacancyhas occurred among the members.oftheBoard of Directors as a result of death,
            resignation, removal or otherwise, the vacancy may be filled by the affinnative vote of a majority
            of the remaining Directors though less than a quorum of the Board of Directors.

                    Section 4.     General Powers as to Neg◊tiable Paper. The Board of Directors may, from
            time to time, authorize the making, signature or endorsement of ch9cks, drafts~ notes and other
            negotiable paper or other instruments for the payment of money and designate the persons who
            will be authorized to make, sign or endorse the same on behalf of the Corporation.

                    Section 5.     Powers as to Other Documents. All material contracts, coiweyances ai1d
            other instruments may be executed on behalf of the Corporation by the President or any Vice
            President, and, if necessary, attested by the Secretary or the Treasurer.

                                                   ARTICLE III
                                                     Officers

        Section 1.     Election or Appointment. The Board of Directors will elect a President, a
Secretary and a Treasurer of the Corporation at each annual meeting and may elect a Vice
President, Assistant Secretary and Assistant Treasurer. The same person may hold any two or more
offices, but no officer will execute; acknowledge or verify any instrument in more than one
capacity. The Directors may also appoint any other officers and agents as they deem neces&ary for
accomplishing the purposes of the Corporation.

        Section 2.      Term of Office. The tenn of office of all officers will commence upon their
election or appointment and will continue until the next annual meeting of the Corporation and
until their respective successors are chosen or until their resignation or removal. Any officer may
be removed from office at any meeting of the Directors, with or without cause, by the affirmative
vote of a majority of the Directors then in office, whenever in their judgment the best interest of
the Corporation will be served.

        An officer may resign by written notice to the Corporation. The resignation will be
effective upon its receipt by the Corporation or at a subsequent time specified in the notice of the
resignation.

       Section 3.     Compensation. Any officer who is an employee of the Corporation will
receive reasonable compensation forhis or l1er services as fixed by the Board of Directors.

        Section 4.     President. The President will be the chief executive officer of the
Corporation and will have general and active management of the activities of the Corporation.The
President will see that all orders and resolutions of the Board of Directors are carried into effect.
The President will execute all i:tuthorized conveyances, contracts or other obligations in the name
of the Corporation except where required by law to be otherwise signed and executed and except
where thy signh1g and execution is exptessly delegated by the .Directors to some other person. The
President will preside at meetings of the Dfrectors and in his or her absence, the Directors present
at the meeting will designate another presiding officer.

        Section 5.     Vice President. The Vice President will, in the absence or disability of the
President, perform the duties and exercise the powers of the President and will perform any other
duties prescribed by the Board of Directors or the President.

                                    CITY OF PONTIAC
                               CITY COUNCIL RESOLUTION

        A RESOLUTION TO HOLD PUBLIC HEARING AND AUTHORIZE
 THE 30-DAY PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD FOR THE 2026 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN
  FOR THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) AND HOME
             INVESTMENT PARTNERSHIPS (HOME) PROGRAMS


WHEREAS, the City of Pontiac is an entitlement community eligible to receive federal
Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and HOME Investment Partnerships Program
(HOME) funds from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD); and,

WHEREAS, HUD regulations require the City to prepare and submit an Annual Action Plan
outlining the proposed use of federal entitlement funds for Program Year 2026; and,

WHEREAS, the City has prepared a draft 2026 Annual Action Plan, which includes a proposed
budget and activities funded through the estimated allocation of $1,399,738.00 in CDBG funds
and $428,550.91 in HOME funds; and,

WHEREAS, the draft 2026 Annual Action Plan will be made available for public review and
comment for a 30-day period beginning June 16, 2026, through July 16, 2026, in accordance with
HUD regulations and the City's Citizen Participation Plan; and,

WHEREAS, a duly noticed public hearing was held on June 16, 2026, during a regular City
Council meeting to solicit public comments regarding the proposed activities and funding
allocations contained within the 2026 Annual Action Plan; and,

WHEREAS, the City has complied with the applicable requirements of the Housing and
Community Development Act of 1974, as amended, and all related federal regulations; now,

THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the City Council of the City of Pontiac hereby authorizes
the release of the draft 2026 Annual Action Plan for the required 30-day public comment period;
and further

RESOLVED, the City Council welcomes and encourages public participation during the public
review and comment period; and further

RESOLVED, that the City shall continue to comply with all applicable federal laws, regulations,
and program requirements in the administration and implementation of the activities identified in
the 2026 Annual Action Plan.

                 Lighting project.

CITY COUNCIL RESOLUTION SUMMARY:

 RESOLUTION TITLE                   DTE Energy City Hall Parking Lot Lighting Project
 DEPARTMENT                         Department of Public Works
 CONTRACT NUMBER(S)
 TYPE                               Standard DTE Energy Agreement
 CONTRACT TERM                     Fiscal Year 26
 RENEWAL OPTIONS                   No Renewal Options
 FUNDING SOURCE                     DPW
 GL FUNDING SOURCE                  101-458-818-000
 TOTAL NOT-TO-
                                   $98,067.93
 EXCEED AMOUNT
Overview
The City Hall Parking Lot Lighting project will totally rehabilitate the antiquated and obsolete parking lot
lighting in the main parking lot and street lighting along Hill Street. Results of the project will improve safety,
visibility, and accessibility in the main parking area and along Hill Street as well as result in a reduction in
annual energy expenses due to LED lighting fixture being installed. The project will also provide a much
more reliable lighting system, and preventative as well as routine maintenance activities will become the
responsibility of DTE Energy.


                                CITY OF PONTIAC CITY COUNCIL

 RESOLUTION TO ENTER INTO CONTRACT AGREEMENT WITH DTE ENERGY FOR THE
                CITY HALL PARKING LOT LIGHTING PROJECT


WHEREAS, DTE Energy has provided the City a proposal to rehabilitate the existing City Hall Parking
Lot Lighting; and,

WHEREAS, the total cost of the project is $98,067.93; and,

WHEREAS, DTE Energy will administer all phases of the project including all labor, equipment and
materials ; and,

WHEREAS, funding budgeted in GL 101-458-818-000; and,

WHEREAS, the DTE Energy Agreement- DTE Work Order Number 76037088 outlines the terms and
responsibilities of the project; now,

THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Pontiac City Council hereby approves the DTE Energy City
Hall Parking Lot Lighting project and authorizes the Department of Public Works Director to execute the
agreement and any related documents.

   13. Special Order Material Terms:

All or a portion of the Equipment consists of special order material: (check one) □ YES     NO

If “Yes” is checked, Customer and Company agree to the following additional terms.

       A.      Customer acknowledges that all or a portion of the Equipment is Special Order
Materials (“SOM”) and not Company’s standard stock. Customer will purchase and stock
replacement SOM and spare parts as provided in Section B below. When replacement equipment
or spare parts are installed from Customer’s inventory, Company will credit Customer in the
amount of the then-current material cost of Company standard street lighting equipment in lieu of
which the SOM is being used. Customer has up to twenty-four (24) months from the time
Company uses, or takes possession of, such Customer SOM to seek reimbursement from
Company.

         B.       Customer will maintain an inventory of at least ___ posts and ___ luminaires and
any other materials agreed to by Company and Customer, and will replenish the stock by ordering
materials no later than thirty (30) calendar days after the materials are drawn from inventory.
Costs of initial inventory are included in this Agreement. If Customer fails to maintain the required
inventory, Company, after 30 days’ notice to Customer, may (but is not required to) order
replacement SOM and Customer will reimburse Company for its costs (including the labor costs
associated with Company’s management of the supply chain for the SOM) no later than thirty (30)
calendar days after receipt of Company’s invoice for such costs. Customer‘s acknowledges that
failure to maintain required inventory could result in extended outages due to SOM lead times.

         C.     The inventory will be stored at _______________________________________.
Access to Customer’s inventory site must be provided between the hours of 9:00a.m. to 4:00p.m.,
Monday through Friday with the exceptions of federal Holidays. If Company is unable to access
the site during such hours for any reason, Company: (i) shall be relieved from any obligation or
commitment to complete the work as scheduled; and (ii) may, at its option, procure the inventory
itself and have Customer to reimburse Company’s costs for doing so. Customer shall name an
authorized representative to contact regarding inventory: levels, access, usage, transactions, and
provide the following contact information to Company:

        Name: __________________________              Title: ______________________________

        Phone Number:___________________              Email: _____________________________

        Customer will immediately notify Company of any changes in the Authorized Customer
Representative. Customer must comply with SOM manufacturer’s recommended inventory
storage guidelines and practices. Damaged SOM will not be installed by Company.

       D.      In the event that SOM is damaged by a third party, Company may (but is not
required to) pursue a damage claim against such third party for all of Company’s costs incurred
because of the claim, including all labor and replacement materials. Company will notify
Customer as to whether Company will pursue such claim within a reasonable time of the SOM
being damaged.

       E.       In the event that SOM becomes obsolete, discontinued, or incompatible with
Company’s infrastructure, Customer shall select new alternate SOM that is compatible with
Company’s then-existing infrastructure. If Customer does not select compatible alternate SOM,
Company reserves the right to select compatible SOM that is, in its reasonable judgment,
substantially similar, or replace the SOM with standard materials, in either case being entitled to


                                  Purchase Agreement – Page 3


reimbursement from Customer for Company’s costs in providing such transition of supply
(including internal overhead and labor costs).

         F.      Should Customer experience, in Company’s reasonable judgment, excessive LED
equipment failures that are not supported by LED manufacturer warranties, Company will replace
the LED equipment with other Company supported Solid State or High Intensity Discharge
luminaires at Company’s discretion. The full cost to complete these replacements to standard
street lighting equipment will be the responsibility of Customer.

Pontiac City Hall Lighting Upgrade




                                 May 13, 2026


      City Hall Lighting Upgrade – Overview
      This City Hall lighting upgrade strengthens the partnership between DTE and
      the City of Pontiac while improving safety, visibility, and accessibility in
      the main parking area and along Hill Street. The project delivers immediate
      benefits to residents, staff, and visitors and establishes a foundation for
      addressing aging city-owned lighting infrastructure. It also positions
      DTE and the City to identify priorities and advance long-term, citywide
      streetlighting improvements that support safety, reliability, and
      community growth.

TO:          Honorable City Council President and City Council

FROM:        Jo Darby, Director of Communications

CC:          Mayor Mike McGuinness and Deputy Mayor Richard T. Seay

DATE:        June 16, 2026

RE:          Resolution Approving Contract with CKS Service for Audio Visual Engineering


CITY COUNCIL RESOLUTION SUMMARY

  Resolution Title       Resolution for Council Chambers AudioNisual Upgrades and
                         Reconfiguration

  Department             Communications

  Division               Cable

  Type                   Sole Source

  Primary Vendor         CKS Service


  Funding Source         Cable Fund - GL 231-291-977.014

  Contract Term          Project-Specific, Until Project Completion

  Option Years           Not applicable



CKS Service will implement an updated automation system and reconfigure existing audio
equipment and access points within the Council Chambers and Cable Control Room to enable real-
time adjustments during meetings and live recordings. This is a sole source contract, and the
vendor has the specialized familiarity with the AudioNisual Engineering configurations of the
Council Chambers and Cable Control Room, due to their ongoing work and existing engagement
with the City of Pontiac. This work will establish a cohesive technology ecosystem between the
Cable Control Room and Council Chambers, advancing the City's long-term plan for continued
upgrades to production technology infrastructure in both facilities. The total cost of this contract
is $22,785, to be funded through Cable Funds. GL 231-291-977.014 Video Equipment.

In accordance with City purchasing policy, contracts valued at $10,000 or more require City
Council approval prior to execution. The Administration recommends Council approve this
contract with CKS Service and authorize execution.


                                  CITY OF PONTIAC CITY COUNCIL

     RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING CONTRACT WITH CKS SERVICE FOR
   AUDIONISUAL RECONFIGURATION SERVICES FOR COUNCIL CHAMBERS
                   AND CABLE CONTROL ROOM

WHEREAS, the City of Pontiac operates Cable access facilities, including the Council Chambers and Cable
Room, which require functional and up-to-date production technology infrastructure to support public meetings
and live recordings; and,

WHEREAS, the existing audio/visual systems within the Council Chambers and Cable Control Room require
reconfiguration to improve operational efficiency and enable real-time adjustments during meetings and live
broadcasts; and,

WHEREAS, CKS Service has been identified as a sole source provider for these services as the original installer
of the City's audio/visual system, possessing proprietary knowledge of the existing equipment and configuration,
engaging an alternative vendor would risk system incompatibility, potential loss of warranty coverage, project
complications, and significant loss of time; and,

WHEREAS, CKS Service has submitted a, qualified quote to implement an updated automation system and
reconfigure existing audio equipment and access points within the Council Chambers and Cable Control Room
and this sole source contract provides the City of Pontiac with the ability to utilize the vendor that has the existing,
specialized familiarity with the challenging current configurations of the audio/visual engineering within Council
Chambers and the Cable Control Room; and,

WHEREAS, this project will establish a cohesive technology ecosystem between the Cable Control Room and
Council Chambers, and supports the City's long-term plan for continued upgrades to production technology
infrastructure in both facilities; and,

WHEREAS, the Pontiac City Council has previously approved a budget amendment appropriating $22,785 from
Cable Funds for the purpose of funding said services; and,

WHEREAS, pursuant to City purchasing policy, contracts valued at $10,000 or more require prior approval of
the City Council before execution; and,

WHEREAS, the funding sources for this project are GL Account 231-291-977.014: Cable Funds and is funded
by previously approved budget amendments approved by City Council; now,

THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Pontiac City Council hereby authorizes the Mayor or his designee
to enter into a contract with CKS Service for professional audio/visual engineering reconfiguration services in an
amount not to exceed $22,785.

                                  OFFICIAL MEMORANDUM

TO:            Honorable City Council President and City Council Members
FROM:          Larry Sirls, Director, Department of Public Works
CC:            Mike McGuinness, Mayor and Richard T. Seay, Deputy Mayor
DATE:          June 16, 2026
RE:            Resolution Authorizing Reimbursement Request Under Oakland County's 2026 West
               Nile Virus Prevention Reimbursement Program

CITY COUNCIL RESOLUTION SUMMARY:
                                Resolution Authorizing Reimbursement Request Under Oakland
                                County's 2026 West Nile Virus Prevention Reimbursement
 RESOLUTION TITLE               Program
 DEPARTMENT                     Department of Public Works
 CONTRACT
 NUMBER(S)                      NIA - Reimbursement Program
 TYPE                           Reimbursement Agreement
 CONTRACT TERM                  NIA
 RENEWAL OPTIONS                No Renewal Options
                                Oakland County West Nile Virus Prevention Reimbursement
 FUNDING SOURCE                 Program
 GL FUNDING SOURCE              NIA
 TOTAL NOT-TO-
 EXCEED AMOUNT                  $7,886.16

Overview
Oakland County has established a West Nile prevention reimbursement program. The City of
Pontiac is eligible for $7,886.16 in funds this year. The City has developed a 2026 mosquito control
program that includes the application of larvicide in catch basins throughout Pontiac and the
distribution of personal insect repellent to residents. The total cost for the City's proposed program
for 2026 is $7,886.16. City Council approval of this resolution is required by Oakland County to
qualify for reimbursement under the 2026 West Nile Virus Prevention Reimbursement Program.

Recommendation
Department of Public Works staff recommend that the City Council approve this resolution
authorizing the Director of the Department of Public Works to act as agent for the City of Pontiac in
requesting reimbursement of eligible mosquito control activities in an amount not to exceed
$7,886.16 under Oakland County's 2026 West Nile Virus Prevention Reimbursement Program.


                         CITY OF PONTIAC CITY COUNCIL

 RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING REIMBURSEMENT REQUEST UNDER
    OAKLAND COUNTY'S 2026 WEST NILE VIRUS PREVENTION
               REIMBURSEMENT PROGRAM

WHEREAS, upon the recommendation of the Oakland County Executive, the Oakland County
Board of Commissioners has established a West Nile Virus Prevention Reimbursement Program
to assist Oakland County cities, villages, and townships in addressing mosquito control activities;
and,
WHEREAS, Oakland County's West Nile Virus Prevention Reimbursement Program authorizes
Oakland County cities, villages, and townships to apply for reimbursement of eligible expenses
incurred in connection with personal mosquito protection measures, habitat eradication,
larviciding, or allowable related activities in designated community areas; and,
WHEREAS, the City of Pontiac will be incurring expenses in the summer of 2026 in connection
with mosquito control activities, including the application of larvicide in catch basins throughout
the City and the distribution of personal insect repellent to residents, believed to be eligible for
reimbursement under Oakland County's 2026 West Nile Virus Prevention Reimbursement
Program; and,
WHEREAS, the total expenditures for eligible mosquito control activities shall not exceed
$7,886.16, consistent with the reimbursement amount allocated to the City of Pontiac for the 2026
program year; and,
WHEREAS, City Council approval of this resolution is required by Oakland County as a
condition of reimbursement under the 2026 West Nile Virus Prevention Reimbursement Program;
now,

THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Pontiac City Council hereby authorizes and directs
the Director of the Department of Public Works to act on behalf of the City of Pontiac, in the
manner and to the extent provided under the Oakland County Board of Commissioners'
Miscellaneous Resolution, to request reimbursement of eligible mosquito control activities under
Oakland County's 2026 West Nile Virus Prevention Reimbursement Program; and further
RESOLVED, that the total expenditures for eligible mosquito control activities shall not exceed
Seven Thousand, Eight Hundred Eighty-Six Dollars and Sixteen Cents ($7,886.16), consistent
with the reimbursement amount allocated to the City of Pontiac for the 2026 program year.


                                  Eligible &Ineligible Expenditures

Eligible Expenditures
• Larvicide for catch basins, retention ponds, etc. (product only)

• Larvicide for distribution to residents (pre-packaged larvicide must be distributed as packaged)

• Personal insect repellent for distribution to residents (eligible products must contain DEET, Picaridin,
  IR3535, Oil of Lemon Eucalyptus, para-menthane-diol, or permethrin as the active ingredient). Product
  purchased must be individual-sized (wipes or lotion/sprays in 6 oz or smaller containers).

      • Consider providing insect repellent products during local festivals, to parks & recreation
        programs, and senior centers

      • Distribute repellent products to multiple locations
Ineligible Expenditures
• Cost of staff time, overtime or equipment used to distribute larvicide

• Adulticide

• Cost of protective clothing, boots, etc.

• Clean-up days, dumpster rentals, etc.

• Citronella candles, yard foggers, bug zappers, coils, lamps or similar items

• Health educational materials

• Local newsletter

If you have questions regarding product eligibility, contact Signa Metivier at metiviers@oakgov.com before ordering.

Good afternoon, Allan, the vast majority of the municipalities use a product called Altosid XR briquettes ingot
shape.
One briquette lasts up to 150 days so it's basically one per catch basin per season.

Finance Department

TO:            Honorable Pontiac City Council

FROM:          Robert J.F. Widigan, Finance Director

CC:            Mayor McGuinness
               Deputy Mayor Richard T. Seay

DATE:          June 16, 2026

RE:            Resolution Authorizing the City Clerk to Publish Notice of a Q4 Fiscal Year-
               End Budget Amendment (FY 2025-2026 True-Up)


The Finance Department is submitting the attached resolution authorizing the City Clerk to publish
notice of a Q4 fiscal year-end budget amendment for FY 2025-2026. This is a year-end true-up.
First, it provides General Fund transfers to bring whole the funds projected to close the fiscal year
in a deficit position; and second, it increases appropriations in the departments and funds projected
to end the year with expenditures over their adopted appropriations. Each adjustment is offset
within the affected fund by available fund balance, revenues not previously appropriated, or an
operating transfer in. In total, the amendment adds an estimated $6,055,000.00 in appropriation
authority across the affected funds - $2,035,000.00 in General Fund transfers to deficit funds and
$4,020,000.00 in direct appropriation increases. The amendment is summarized below:

   •   All current funds projected to end FY 2025-2026 in a deficit position - estimated
       total: $2,035,000.00
   •   All current expenditures projected to end FY 2025-2026 exceeding appropriations -
       estimated total: $4,020,000.00




                                                      1


Summary-Use of Fund Balance by Fund:
                                                                                       Fund Balance Used
 Fund 101 - General Fund                                                                     $2,310,000.00
 Fund 232 - VEBA Retiree Healthcare Opt Out                                                  $3,720,000.00
 Fund 212 - Senior Activities Millage                                                            $25,000.00
 Total Fund Balance Used                                                                     $6,055,000.00
Fund JOI - General Fund use comprises a $135,000.00 operating transfer to the Cable Fund, a $1,900,000.00
operating transfer to the District Court, and $275,000.00 for Waterford Fire Department professional services.

This amendment is required to comply with the City Charter and the Uniform Budgeting and
Accounting Act. Charter Section 5.104 requires that total appropriations not exceed the City's
estimated revenues and that no liabilities be incurred except in accordance with the appropriation
ordinance. The Uniform Budgeting and Accounting Act, Act 2 of 1968 (MCL 141.421 et seq.),
prohibits deficit spending: it bars adopting an appropriations act or amendment that causes total
estimated expenditures, including an accrued deficit, to exceed total estimated revenues and
available surplus (MCL 141.436(7)); prohibits incurring expenditures against an appropriation
account beyond the amount appropriated (MCL 141.438(3)); and requires the legislative body to
amend the appropriations act as soon as a deviation becomes apparent and its amount can be
determined (MCL 141.437(1)).

ORDINANCE


                                     CITY OF PONTIAC
                                       ORDINANCE
                              NON-STORMWATER DISCHARGES


AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND CHAPTER 58, ENVIRONMENT, OF THE CODE OF
ORDINANCES FOR THE CITY OF PONTIAC, NON-STORMWATER DISCHARGES,
IN ORDER TO REGULATE THE DISCHARGE OF NON-STORMWATER
SUBSTANCES AND PROTECT WATER QUALITY STANDARDS IN THE CITY OF
PONTIAC.

THE CITY OF PONTIAC ORDAINS:

Section 1.    Amendment.

Chapter 58, Environment, of the Code of Ordinances for the City of Pontiac, shall be
amended by adding a new Article IX to read as follows:

                        ARTICLE IX. - NON-STORMWATER DISCHARGES

Sec. 58-700. - Definitions.

For the purposes of this article, the words set out shall have the following meanings:

Discharge means the addition of any waste, waste effluent, wastewater, pollutant, or any
combination thereof to any surface water of the state.

Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) means all separate storm sewers that are owned or
operated by the United States, a state, city, township, county, district, association, or other public
body created by or pursuant to state law, having jurisdiction over disposal of sewage, industrial
wastes, storm water, or other wastes, including special districts under state law, such as a sewer
district, flood control district, or drainage district, or similar entity, or a designated or approved
management agency under Section 208 of the Clean Water Act that discharges to the waters of the
state. This term includes systems similar to separate storm sewer systems in municipalities, such
as systems at military bases, large hospital or prison complexes, and highways and thoroughfares.
The term does not include separate storm sewers in very discrete areas, such as individual buildings.

NP DES means National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System.

Storm water means storm water runoff, snow melt runoff, surface runoff and drainage, and non-
storm water included under the conditions of this article.


 Waters of the State means any of the following: groundwater; lakes, including the Great Lakes
 bordering the state; rivers; streams; all other water courses and bodies of water within the
 jurisdiction of the state, including wetlands as defined by Part 303 of the Act, wetlands
 protection, being SS324.30301 to 324.30323 of the Michigan Compiled Laws.

 Sec. 58-701. - Unauthorized discharges.

 a)    No person shall discharge or cause to be discharged into the MS4 or waters of the state
       of any materials, including but not limited to pollutants or waters containing any
       pollutants that cause or contribute to a violation of applicable water quality standards,
       other than storm water. The commencement, conduct, or continuance of any illicit
       discharge to the MS4 is prohibited; however, the following discharges are excluded from
       prohibition as described so long as they are identified as not being a significant
       contributor of pollutants to the waters of the state:

                 (1)   Water line flushing and discharges from potable water sources;

                (2)    Landscape irrigation runoff, lawn watering runoff, and irrigation waters;

                (3)    Diverted stream flows and flows from riparian habitats or wetlands;

                (4)    Rising groundwaters and springs;

                (5)    Uncontaminated groundwater infiltration and seepage;

                (6)    Uncontaminated pumped groundwater, except for groundwater
                       cleanups specifically authorized by NPDES permits;

                (7)    Foundation drains, water from crawl space pumps, footing drains,
                       and basement sumps;

                (8)    Air conditioning condensation;

                (9)    Waters from noncommercial car washing;

               (10)    Street wash water; and

               (11)    Dechlorinated swimming pool water from single, two and three
                       family residences.

 b)    Discharges or flows from firefighting activities are not prohibited unless they are
       identified as a significant source of pollutants to the waters of the state.

Sec. 58-702. - Prohibition of illicit connections.

       a) The construction, use, maintenance, or continued existence of illicit connections to the


             storm drain system is prohibited.

        b) This prohibition expressly includes, without limitation, illicit connections made in the past,
           regardless of whether the connection was permissible under law or practices applicable
           or prevailing at the time of connection.

        c) A person is considered to be in violation of this article if the person connects a line
           conveying sewage to a storm drain system or MS4 or allows such a connection to
           continue.

Sec. 58-703. - Prohibition of Direct Dumping or Disposal of Materials into the MS4.

        The direct dumping of materials or discharges into the MS4 is prohibited except for those
        illicit discharges identified as not being a significant contributor to violations of water quality
        standards.

Sec. 58-704. - Right of Entry:

        The City of Pontiac Department of Public Works or other authorized enforcement agency shall
        be permitted to enter upon all properties for the purposes of inspection, observation, measurement,
        sampling and testing of suspected non-stormwater discharges in accordance with the
        provisions of this article. Refusal ofreasonable access to the City and/or representatives of
        the authorized enforcement agency to any part of the premises is a violation of this article.

Section 2.      Repealer.

This Ordinance hereby repeals any ordinances in conflict herewith.


Section 3.      Savings Clause.

That nothing in this Ordinance hereby adopted be construed to affect any just or legal right or
remedy of any character nor shall any just or legal right or remedy of any character be lost,
impaired or affected by this Ordinance.


Section 4.      Severability.

The various parts, Sections and clauses of this Ordinance are declared to be severable. If any
part, sentence, paragraph, Section or clause is adjudged unconstitutional or invalid by a court of
competent jurisdiction, the remainder of the Ordinance shall not be affected.


Section 5.    Adoption and Effective Date.

This Ordinance is hereby declared to have been adopted by the City Council for the City of
Pontiac at a meeting thereof duly called and held on the 16th day of June, -2026, and ordered to
be given effect as mandated by City and statute.

ORDINANCE


                             CITY OF PONTIAC CITY COUNCIL

                           EMERGENCY MUNICIPAL ORDINANCE

AN EMERGENCY INTERIM ZONING ORDINANCE TO AMEND CHAPTER 42,
COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT, OF THE PONTIAC MUNICIPAL CODE TO ADD
ARTICLE XI, TEMPORARY MORATORIUM ON NEW OR EXPANDED DETENTION
FACILITIES, AND TO ESTABLISH A TEMPORARY LAND USE MORATORIUM ON
THE ACCEPTANCE, PROCESSING, AND APPROVAL OF APPLICATIONS FOR NEW
OR EXPANDED DETENTION FACILITIES IN THE CITY OF PONTIAC TO THE
MAXIMUM EXTENT PERMITTED BYLAW

CHAPTER 42, ARTICLE XI. MORATORIUM ON THE ACCEPTANCE, PROCESSING, AND
APPROVAL OF APPLICATIONS FOR NEW OR EXPANDED DETENTION FACILITIES



THE CITY OF PONTIAC ORDAINS:

Add Chapter 42, Article XI, Section 42-258. Purpose and Findings
   A. The City of Pontiac has determined that an emergency interim zoning ordinance is necessary to
      ensure that the City has adequate time to study and consider appropriate zoning and land use
      regulations for new or expanded detention facilities within the City.

   B. The City has a substantial interest in protecting the public peace, property, health, safety, and
      welfare of its residents, and in ensuring the orderly development and use of land within the
      City. The City has further determined that new or expanded detention facilities may create
      significant land use impacts, including, but not limited to, impacts on public safety, emergency
      services, transportation, parking, construction staging, utilities, water and sewer capacity,
      wastewater systems, public health, and compatibility with surrounding land uses.

   C. The City Code and Zoning Ordinance do not currently contain regulations specifically
      addressing detention facilities as a separate land use. The City has determined that additional
      study is necessary to evaluate whether and how detention facilities should be regulated through
      the City's zoning and development review processes, including the appropriate zoning districts,
      approval standards, site design requirements, public safety access, buffering, parking, traffic
      circulation, utility impacts, and other land use considerations.

   D. The City has considered the consequences of having no moratorium, but has determined that a
      temporary moratorium is necessary to preserve the status quo while the City studies and
      considers appropriate zoning and land use regulations for detention facilities. The City further
      finds that an emergency ordinance is necessary because delay could result in the filing,


      acceptance, processing, or approval of applications for new or expanded detention facilities
      before the City has adequate regulations to evaluate the land use impacts of such facilities.

   E. This Ordinance is adopted as an emergency interim zoning and land use regulation and shall
      temporarily supplement the City of Pontiac Zoning Ordinance and all City application, permit,
      site plan, special exception, certificate of use, occupancy, building, and development approval
      procedures for the duration of the moratorium.

   F. This Ordinance is intended to operate as an interim zoning and land use regulation. It is not
      intended to regulate detention operations, custody decisions, immigration enforcement,
      criminal justice operations, conditions of confinement, or the internal operations of any federal,
      state, county, or other governmental entity.

Add Chapter 42, Article XI, Section 42-259. Moratorium

   A. The City hereby places a temporary moratorium on the acceptance, processing, review, or
      approval of any application, permit, site plan, special exception permit, zoning approval,
      building permit, occupancy permit, certificate of use, temporary use permit, or other
      development approval for the establishment of a new detention facility or the expansion of an
      existing detention facility within the City of Pontiac.

   B. During the moratorium, no City department, official, employee, board, commission, or body
      shall accept, process, review, approve, or issue any application, permit, approval, or
      authorization for the establishment of a new detention facility or the expansion of an existing
      detention facility, whether the proposed use is principal or accessory, and whether the proposed
      use is permanent or temporary.

   C. For purposes of this Ordinance, "expansion" means an increase in the size, area, capacity,
      number of beds, intensity, quantity, or scope of an existing detention facility use.

   D. Any application or request submitted during the moratorium that seeks approval for a use or
      activity prohibited by this Ordinance shall not be accepted or processed. Any application
      accepted as a result of error, omission, vague description, or incomplete or inaccurate
      information shall be null and void and shall have no legal force or effect.

Add Chapter 42, Article XI, Section 42-260. Moratorium Term.

   A. The moratorium established by this Ordinance shall remain in effect for a period of one (1)
      year from the effective date of this Ordinance, unless repealed, shortened, or extended by
      subsequent action of the City Council as permitted by law.

   B. During the moratorium, the City Administration, Planning Division, and any other appropriate
      City officials or consultants shall study and make recommendations concerning permanent
      zoning and land use regulations for detention facilities. The study may include, but is not
      limited to, analysis of the following:

      1. The potential land use impacts of detention facilities;
      2. Appropriate zoning districts for detention facilities, if any;
      3. Whether detention facilities should be permitted as a principal permitted use, special
         exception use, conditional use, or other regulated use;
      4. Site design, access, circulation, parking, loading, security, buffering, screening, lighting,
         utility, water, sewer, wastewater, emergency access, and public safety considerations;


       5. Construction staging and temporary impacts associated with the development or expansion
          of detention facilities;
       6. The relationship between detention facilities and surrounding residential, commercial,
          industrial, institutional, civic, and public uses;
       7. Whether different types of detention facilities should be regulated differently based on their
          land use impacts; and
       8. Any other zoning, planning, public safety, infrastructure, or land use considerations
          determined to be relevant.

   C. No later than nine (9) months after the effective date of this Ordinance, the Mayor or designee
      shall transmit the results of the study, together with any recommended ordinance amendments,
      to the City Council for consideration.

Add Chapter 42, Article XI, Section 42-261. Definition
   A. For purposes of this Ordinance only, "detention facility" means a facility used for the secure
      confinement of persons who are detained pending adjudication, detained pending civil
      immigration proceedings, or serving a sentence of incarceration.

   B. For purposes of this Ordinance only, "detention facility" does not include:

   C. A facility operated solely for the detention of juveniles for rehabilitative, counseling, treatment,
      mental health, educational, or medical services under the jurisdiction of the Michigan Family
      Court or the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services;

   D. A temporary holding cell within a police station or courthouse used exclusively for pre-
      arraignment, in-custody court appearances, or other temporary law enforcement or court-
      related custody lasting less than seventy-two (72) hours;

   E. An influx care facility for unaccompanied noncitizen children operated by the United States
      Department of Health and Human Services Office of Refugee Resettlement; or

   F. A receiving center for commercially sexually exploited children under Michigan law, MCL
      712B.1 et seq.

   G. For purposes of this Ordinance only, the terms ''jail" and ''jail farm," wherever used in the
      Pontiac City Code or Zoning Ordinance, shall be treated as detention facilities.

Add Chapter 42, Article XI, Section 42-262. Existing Lawful Uses; Governmental Uses;
Preemption Savings Clause

   A. This Ordinance shall not prohibit the lawful continuation, maintenance, or repair of any vested
      and otherwise lawfully established use, structure, or development existing as of the effective
      date of this Ordinance, provided that such use, structure, or development is not expanded
      during the moratorium.

   B. This Ordinance is intended to regulate land use and development approvals to the maximum
      extent permitted by law. Nothing in this Ordinance shall be interpreted or applied to regulate
      the conditions of confinement, detention operations, immigration enforcement, criminal justice
      operations, law enforcement operations, or any federal, state, county, or other governmental
      function in a manner preempted by state or federal law.


    C. Nothing in this Ordinance shall be construed to prohibit, restrict, or impair a federal, state,
       county, or other governmental entity from carrying out a governmental function where the City
       lacks authority to apply its zoning or land use regulations under applicable law.

    D. Nothing in this Ordinance shall be construed to prohibit ordinary maintenance, repairs, life-
       safety work, security improvements, code compliance work, or other work required to protect
       health, safety, or welfare at an existing lawful facility, provided such work does not expand the
       detention facility use unless otherwise required by law.

    E. To the extent any application of this Ordinance to a particular facility, person, governmental
       entity, or circumstance would be preempted by state or federal law, or would otherwise be
       unenforceable under applicable law, the Ordinance shall be applied only to the maximum
       extent permitted by law, and the invalid or preempted application shall not affect the validity or
       enforceability of this Ordinance in any other respect.

Add Chapter 42, Article XI, Section 42-263. Validity and Severability

    A. If any section, subsection, sentence, clause, phrase, word, or application of this Ordinance is
       held invalid, unconstitutional, unenforceable, or preempted by state or federal law, such
       holding shall not affect the validity of the remaining portions or applications of this Ordinance,
       which shall remain in full force and effect.

Add Chapter 42, Article XI, Section 42-264. Conflict with Other Ordinances

    A. All ordinances or parts of ordinances in conflict with this Ordinance are repealed only to the
        extent necessary to give this Ordinance full force and effect during the moratorium term.

Add Chapter 42, Article XI, Section 42-265. Emergency Clause and Effective Date

    A. The City Council finds and declares that an emergency exists because any delay in the effective
       date of this Ordinance could allow the acceptance, processing, review, or approval of
       applications for new or expanded detention facilities before the City has adequate zoning and
       land use regulations to evaluate the impacts of such facilities on the public peace, property,
       health, safety, and welfare.

    B. This Ordinance is declared to be an emergency ordinance necessary for the immediate
       preservation of the public peace, property, health, safety, and welfare of the City of Pontiac.

    C. This Ordinance shall become effective immediately upon adoption as authorized by Section
       3.l 12(e) of the City of Pontiac Home Rule Charter.

Overview

The City of Pontiac has acquired the 300 W. Huron Building and the Department of Public Works
requires technology infrastructure upgrades to bring the facility to City operational standards.

The project addresses four areas: camera systems (interior and exterior), door access control,
structured cabling, and IT hardware. All vendors are currently under contract with the City and have
been sourced through the City's procurement process.
 Scope                             Vendor                                        Amount
 Camera Systems                    DIA Central                                   $225,230.00
 Door Access Systems               DIA Central                                   $75,450.00
 Structured Cabling                BND (Best Network Design)                     $75,000.00
 IT Hardware                       Insight Public Sector Inc.                    $128,552.11
 Total Not-to-Exceed                                                             $504,232.11


Funding
Funding for the 300 W. Huron Technology Improvements is budgeted in GL Account No. 101-458-
818-000. The total project cost shall not exceed $504,232.11.
These investments in facility and campus security are prudent in order to protect the structure, the
grounds, employees, the visitors, the equipment, and more. It is also a cost-effective mesasure to
proactively address property liability, verifying or refuting any claims made agains the City of
Pontiac related to our property, equipment, and operations.


Recommendation
The Department of Public Works recommends that the City Council approve the vendor agreements
with DIA Central, BND, and Insight Public Sector Inc. for technology upgrades at 300 W. Huron
and authorize the IT Director and Director of Public Works to execute all agreements and related
documents.

                                    CITY OF PONTIAC
                                 OFFICIAL MEMORANDUM


TO:           Honorable City Council President and City Council Members
FROM:         Larry Sirls, Director, Department of Public Works
CC:           Mike McGuinness, Mayor and Richard T. Seay, Deputy Mayor
DATE:         June 16, 2026
RE:           Approve Construction Engineering Services Agreement with Hubbell, Roth &
              Clark, Inc. for Citywide Safety Improvements and Kennett Road Safety
              Improvements


CITY COUNCIL RESOLUTION SUMMARY:
                                       Resolution to Approve Construction Engineering Services
                                       Agreement with Hubbell, Roth & Clark, Inc. for Citywide
                                       Safety Improvements and Kennett Road Safety
RESOLUTION TITLE                       Improvements
DEPARTMENT                             Department of Public Works
CONTRACT NUMBER                        Job No. 20240693
TYPE                                   Standard Agreement
CONTRACT TERM                         NIA
RENEWAL OPTIONS                       NIA
FUNDING SOURCE                        Major Street Fund
GL FUNDING SOURCE                      202-451-97 4.000
TOTAL NOT-TO-EXCEED
AMOUNT                                 $265,648.00

Overview
The City of Pontiac was awarded $1,887,840 in Federal Highway Safety Improvement Program
(HSIP) funds, with the City contributing $387,840 as its required 20% local match. The low bid for
construction was received on May 1, 2026, for $1,688,273.29 from Dan's Excavating, Inc. The
project encompasses two improvement packages:
   •   Citywide Safety Improvements: Centerpoint Parkway at Ring Road signal modernization;
       Walton Boulevard HA WK pedestrian hybrid beacon with median refuge island (Colony
       Lane to Greenwood Lane); and sign upgrades on Edison Street at Howard, Chamberlain,
       Lewis, Kemp, and Whitfield Streets.
   •   Kennett Road Safety Improvements: Signal modernizations at Kennett Road &
       Elementary School and Kennett Road & Stanley Avenue; removal of pedestrian bridge on
       Kennett Road; wet reflective pavement markings from City Limit to Baldwin; and sign


       upgrades at Sarasota Avenue, Cherrylawn Drive, Cloverlawn Drive, and Meadowlawn
       Drive.
To administer the project in accordance with MDOT Local Agency Program (LAP) requirements,
a Construction Engineering proposal was requested from Hubbell, Roth & Clark, Inc. (HRC). HRC
will provide complete contract administration, MDOT office technician/clerk services,
AASHTOWare reporting, wage reviews, construction engineering, record drawings, construction
layout/staking, on-site observation, and materials testing.

Funding
HSIP funds cover 80% of construction; the City's 20% share ($387,840) and CE services
($265,648) are funded through the Major Street Fund, GL No. 202-451-974.000. HRC's fee
includes $240,648 in direct labor and $25,000 in subconsultant costs for mast arm fabrication and
anchor bolt testing.

Recommendation
Department of Public Works recommends approval of the HRC Construction Engineering
agreement not to exceed $265,648 to ensure proper construction oversight, MDOT LAP
compliance, and federal closeout for both improvement projects.


                         CITY OF PONTIAC CITY COUNCIL

    RESOLUTION TO APPROVE A CONSTRUCTION ENGINEERING SERVICES
  AGREEMENT WITH HUBBELL, ROTH & CLARK, INC. FOR CITYWIDE SAFETY
       IMPROVEMENTS AND KENNETT ROAD SAFETY IMPROVEMENTS


WHEREAS, at its regular meeting, the City of Pontiac was awarded $1,887,840 in Federal
Highway Safety Improvement Program funds for the Citywide Safety Improvements and Kennett
Road Safety Improvements projects, with the City responsible for a $387,840 participatory share;
and,
WHEREAS, the low bid for construction was received on May 1, 2026, from Dan's Excavating,
Inc. in the amount of $1,688,273.29; and,
WHEREAS, the Michigan Department of Transportation (MDOT) requires the project to be
administered in accordance with the MDOT Local Agency Program (LAP); and,
WHEREAS, a Construction Engineering proposal was requested from Hubbell, Roth & Clark,
Inc. (HRC) to provide contract administration, on site observation, construction staking, materials
testing, record drawings, and all required MDOT LAP compliance services; and,
WHEREAS, HRC proposes to complete these Construction Engineering Services for a not-to-
exceed fee of $265,648, to be billed monthly on a time and material basis in accordance with
HRC's current City contract; and,
WHEREAS, funding for these Construction Engineering Services is budgeted in GL Account
202-451-974.000; now,
THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Pontiac City Council hereby approves the
Construction Engineering Services agreement with Hubbell, Roth & Clark, Inc. for the Citywide
Safety Improvements and Kennett Road Safety Improvements projects; and further
RESOLVED, that the City Council authorizes a total contract amount not to exceed Two Hundred
Sixty-Five Thousand, Six Hundred Forty-Eight Dollars ($265,648.00), inclusive of all direct labor,
materials testing, and subconsultant costs; and further
RESOLVED, that the Director of Public Works is authorized to execute all agreements and
documents necessary to implement this resolution, and that the Mayor or his Designee and the City
Clerk are authorized to take all actions required to carry out its intent.

Overview
Fleis & VandenBrink Engineering, Inc. (F&V) has submitted a proposal dated April 28, 2026, to provide Traffic
Engineering Services to the City of Pontiac. The proposal was developed following a meeting with City staff
on January 13, 2026, during which the City identified four key areas requiring traffic engineering support to
improve public safety and operational effectiveness. The scope of services is organized into four components
as follows:


                Scope Item                                          Description                                   Fee
                                           Comprehensive review of existing fire stations and service
                                           areas; recommendations for new or relocated station sites based
                                           on GIS data, run volumes, demographics, and response time
 A. Fire Station Locations                 coverage                                                          $30,000
                                           Support for City grant applications to fund EVP implementation
 B. Emergency Vehicle Pre-Emption (EVP)    on key corridors, including BUILD, ATTAIN, SS4A, CMAQ,
