 TOTAL                                                                                                       $197,000

Funding


The total amount for all four components is $197,000.00, funded through GL Account No. 101-458-818-000.
The proposal is valid for 60 days from April 28, 2026. Any additional services required beyond the defined
scope will be addressed through a separate Contract Amendment.


Recommendation
Department of Public Works recommends that the City Council approve this resolution authorizing a
Professional Services Agreement with Fleis & V andenBrink Engineering, Inc. in an amount not to exceed
$197,000.00 for Traffic Engineering Services. Approval will allow the City to advance four critical traffic safety
and operations initiatives, including fire station location analysis, emergency vehicle pre-emption grant
preparation, signalized intersection evaluation, and commercial vehicle route planning.

Dear Larry:

The professional staff of Fleis & VandenBrink Engineering, Inc. (F&V) appreciates the opportunity to present
you with our proposal to provide Traffic Engineering Services for the City of Pontiac, Michigan. Our
understanding of the project needs, proposed scope of work, and associated professional fees are outlined
below.

PROJECT UNDERSTANDING
The City of Pontiac identified several key areas where they are looking for traffic engineering support to
accomplish specific goals regarding operations and safety. The following projects were discussed at our
meeting on January 13, 2026:
A. FIRE STATION LOCATIONS
A comprehensive review of the existing fire stations and the existing service areas. Provide
recommendations for locating new or relocated fire stations to support operations and provide coverage.
B. EMERGENCY VEHICLE PRE-EMPTION (EVP)
Provide support for the City regarding the data necessary for grant applications to implement EVP on key
corridors where the technology would be the most impactful.
C. SIGNALIZED INTERSECTION STUDY
Provide a comprehensive evaluation of the existing signalized intersections in the City and identify potential
locations to remove traffic signals. Provide further analysis and evaluation of the identified intersections to
determine if the signal is warranted.
D. COMMERCIAL VEHICLE ROUTE SIGNAGE
Perform a review of the existing truck routing in the City. Provide recommendations for a comprehensive truck
routing plan to manage local truck activity and reduce impacts on the local community. Recommendation to
include a comprehensive truck routing plan for implementation and enforcement.

Our understanding of the project is based on the information you have provided, a review of the study road
network, and our professional experience. If our understanding of this project does not fully address your
needs, please let us know, and we will modify our proposal accordingly.

SCOPE OF SERVICES
A. FIRE STATION LOCATIONS
A comprehensive review of the existing fire stations and the existing service areas. Provide
recommendations for locating new or relocated fire stations to support operation and provide coverage.
1.    Background Information
      a. Obtain the locations of the existing fire stations from the City of Pontiac. Provide a description of each
         fire station location and its service area, including a site map showing each location.
      b. Obtain historic run volumes at the existing fire station locations. Provide a summary of the existing
         run volumes and locations.
2.    Data Review and Location Assessment
      a. Evaluate historic run volumes and locations and complete an evaluation to determine the preferred
         facility location(s). Use Geographic Information System (GIS) data from the City of Pontiac to review
         the existing available demographic and property information.
      b. Identify potential building sites through the development of ranking criteria through the established
         City/Department goals. Key items in this evaluation and ranking of site includes:
      c. Determine best coverage through evaluation of the established City criteria for population served and
         miles of street covered in the established response time.
              • Population and Demographics serviced
              • Call frequency
              • Existing facility locations (asset management not included in this scope)
              • Available vacant properties in preferred service areas
              • Site preparation and associated costs
              • Site Access
3.   Recommendations Summary
     a. Use the established criteria to prepare a list of potential locations for new or relocated fire stations for
        consideration.
     b. Provide recommendations for locating new or relocated fire stations to support operation and provide
        coverage.
B. EMERGENCY VEHICLE PRE-EMPTION (EVP)
Provide support for the City regarding the data necessary for grant applications to implement EVP on key
corridors where the technology would be the most impactful.
1. Grant Application Assistance
     a.     Work with the City to provide information supporting the grant applications for EVP implementation.
     b.     Several grant opportunities are available for the design and implementation of EVP technology,
            including:
                 • Better Utilizing Investments to Leverage Development (BUILD) Grant: $5M-$25M, 80% grant
                    funded
                 • Advanced Transportation Technology and Innovation (ATTAIN) Grant: $3M-$9M, 80% grant
                    funded
                 • SS4A Planning Grant: $1 M-4M, 80% grant funded
                 • CMAQ Grant: 80% grant funded
                 • HSIP Grant: 80% grant funded, Must have a safety element-reducing crashes through EVP
C. SIGNALIZED INTERSECTION STUDY
Provide a comprehensive evaluation of the existing signalized intersections in the City and identify potential
locations to remove traffic signals. Provide further analysis and evaluation of the identified intersections to
determine if the signal is warranted.
1. Study Area
   a. Obtain information from the City regarding their existing inventory of signalized intersections.
   b. Summarize the signalized intersections by corridor and isolated locations.
   c. Obtain existing available traffic count data on the study corridors and adjacent to the isolated
      locations

      d.    Obtain information from the City regarding the age of the existing signal infrastructure at the
            intersection locations.
      e.    Rank the intersections based upon location, traffic volumes, and the age of the equipment to provide
            a high level determination of which signals intersections may be considered for removal.
     f.     Prepare a list of intersections to be evaluated for consideration of removing the traffic signal. Upon
            review with the City the final list of intersections for evaluation will be determined.
      g.    Conduct a site visit at the selected study intersections and collect a field inventory including the
            existing geometries, lane use, pedestrian facilities and proximity to transit. This proposal includes
            an initial evaluation of up to 10 study intersections, additional intersections can be included in the
            stuy for additional fees.
      h.    Update the list of recommended intersections for considering removal of the traffic signal based upon
            the information obtained in the field reviewed. Prepare the final list for intersection evaluation for City
            review and approval.
2.   Traffic Data Collection
     a. Collect 12-hour turning movement counts at the selected study intersections (6:00 AM to 6:00 PM).
         The data collection will include vehicles (cars, buses, and HV%), pedestrians and bicycle volumes.
         Data collection to be performed during a typical weekday when schools are in session.
3.    Signal Warrant Analysis
      a. Perform a signal warrant analysis at the selected study intersections to determine if the existing traffic
         volumes meet the applicable signal warrant criteria for intersection signalization.
      b. The signal warrant analysis will be performed in accordance with the requirements outlined in the
         Michigan Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MMUTCD).
4.    Recommendations Summary
      a. Provide summary of recommendations to the City that includes the following items
             • Existing signalized intersections to remove.
             • Alternative traffic control measures and signage
             • Other considerations for mitigation measures for multi-modal access and safety
      b. Complete a technical report consistent with accepted standards, which outlines the methodologies,
         analyses, results, and recommendations of the traffic study. Work will follow accepted traffic
         engineering practice and the standards documented by ITE, FHWA, MOOT, and the City of Pontiac.
      c. Upon completion of the proposed scope of work, a draft copy of the study memorandum will be
         provided for internal review and comment. F&V will provide one revision to the memorandum based
         on comments received regarding the draft and finalize the memorandum for submission. An
         electronic copy of the project report will be provided. A hard copy of the project report will be provided
         upon request, subject to an additional fee.
D. COMMERCIAL VEHICLE ROUTE REVIEW
Perform a review of the existing truck routing in the City. Provide recommendations for a comprehensive truck
routing plan to manage local truck activity and reduce impacts on the local community. Recommendation to
include a comprehensive truck routing plan for implementation and enforcement.
1. Background Data
   a. Obtain information from the City regarding their existing approved and restricted truck routes.
   b. Provide a summary of the existing truck restriction signage throughout the City.
   c. Collect heavy truck origin-destination (O-D) data utilizing geospatial telematics data sets (i.e. Replica,
      Geotab)
   d. Provide a summary of the existing truck routing throughout the City.
2.   Truck Route Assessment
     a. Review the City roadway segments that meet the minimum required criteria for a truck route
        destination. This includes the consideration of national functional classification, Act 51 certification,
        bridge vertical clearance, bridge weight limit, and any code restrictions.
     b. Develop a scoring system and rank each roadway segment in the City from the least to the most
        preferred truck routes based on specific criteria. The criteria include adjacer_it land uses, multi-modal
        impacts, environmental (noise, vibration) impact, connectivity, compatibility for truck usages, and
        roadway and bridge conditions.
     c. Prepare a list of potential routes that may be considered for truck routes.

               •   Recommended Route: Designated truck through routes

               development workflows



For the Fiscal Year 2026 Budget Year, funding was allocated to support technology solutions that
enhance the City's economic development operations, reporting capabilities, and compliance
monitoring.

The Economic Vitality Division is requesting approval to enter a contract with CivicServe, Inc.,
the sole-source provider of the CivicServe Economic Development Suite for local governments.
CivicServe offers a centralized, cloud-based platform designed specifically to support the full
economic development lifecycle, including project and incentive management, business retention
and expansion activities, redevelopment agreement administration, compliance tracking, and state
and local reporting requirements.

The platform will enable City staff to streamline economic development workflows, automate
compliance notifications and documentation collection, improve project tracking, maintain
business and property data, and generate real-time reports and analytics. CivicServe also provides


                                                                                                 1


a public-facing portal that improves accessibility and transparency for businesses, developers, and
residents seeking information regarding economic development opportunities and programs.

As documented in the attached sole-source letter (Exhibit A), CivicServe is the only purpose-built
platform that combines these economic development functions into a single integrated solution for
local governments. The software will reduce reliance on manual processes, improve operational
efficiency, strengthen compliance oversight, and support data-driven decision-making.

Based on the information contained herein, the Economic Vitality Division respectfully requests
that the Pontiac City Council approve entering into a contract with CivicServe, Inc. for an amount
not to exceed $18,000 annually from the appropriate budgeted account to provide economic
development management, reporting, and compliance software services in accordance with the
attached proposal and sole-source justification.

    submissions, log and track interactions with businesses and developers, and log site visits & BRE visits with survey
    results.

    residents will be able to supply compliance & KPI documentation directly to the City seamlessly through the public
    portal.
•   Property management portal: Manage available properties, track submissions of interest from the public portal,
    and collect property information from brokers.

    to allow them to understand which programs they are eligible for.

    outreach activity, and more. Assuming the City provides CivicServe the necessary data from its GIS system, the City

    platform. Leverage the system's custom reporting wizard to create complex custom reports to meet local & state
    reporting requirements.

 AMOUNT



Overview
The Courts and Law Enforcement Management Information System (CLEMIS) Authority is a regional
public safety information management system serving approximately 250 governmental entities across
ten counties in Michigan. Originally created by Oakland County in 1968 to enable criminal justice and
public safety agencies to share data electronically, CLEMIS was formally established as a separate
legal entity effective February 1, 2026, pursuant to the Urban Cooperation Act of 1967 and an
Interlocal Agreement between Oakland County, the Charter Township of Bloomfield, and the Ch_arter
Township of White Lake.
The City of Pontiac has an opportunity to join the CLEMIS Authority as a Participating Public Agency,
which will provide the City's Code Enforcement Department with access to the CLEMIS system for
courts and law enforcement management information services. Participation requires City Council
adoption of an Authorizing Resolution, execution of a Participation Agreement, and execution of a
CLEMIS Main Services Agreement (MSA).


Funding
Funding for CLEMIS participation is available through the General Fund. The General Ledger
Number being utilized is 101-733-818.000. The annual cost of $23,301.00 will be payable beginning
October 1, 2026, for the period October 2026 through September 2027. The subscription term renews
automatically on an annual basis unless terminated by either party with at least 30 days' written notice
prior to the expiration of the then-current term.


Recommendation
City Services staff recommend that the City Council approve this resolution authorizing the City of
Pontiac to participate in the CLEMIS Authority Interlocal Agreement and Main Services Agreement,
and authorizing the Director of City Services to execute all necessary documents on behalf of the City.
Approval will allow the City's Code Enforcement Department to access the CLEMIS system beginning
October 1, 2026, supporting improved data sharing and operational efficiency in courts and law
enforcement management information services.


                     CITY OF PONTIAC CITY COUNCIL

   RESOLUTION TO APPROVE PARTICIPATION IN CLEMIS
        AUTHORITY INTERLOCAL AGREEMENT

to 124.512; and,
WHEREAS, the City of Pontiac seeks to participate in the Courts and Law Enforcement
Management Information System (CLEMIS) Authority Interlocal Agreement and enter into a
CLEMIS Main Services Agreement to provide the City's Code Enforcement Department with
access to courts and law enforcement management information services; and,
WHEREAS, the CLEMIS Authority has provided a quote for services for the City's Code
Enforcement Department for Fiscal Year 2027, in the total annual amount of $23,301.00, with the
subscription term renewed automatically on an annual basis; and,
WHEREAS, existing funding within the City's budget has been appropriated that is sufficient for
this expense, and the General Ledger number being utilized is 101-733-818.000; and,
WHEREAS, the City Council finds that participation in the CLEMIS Authority Interlocal

RESOLVED that the Mayor and City Clerk are authorized to execute all documents necessary to

to carry out the intent of this resolution.

Overview

At the February 17, 2026, City Council meeting, Council approved the award of the Galloway
Lake Park Court Improvements contract to WCI Contractors for $295,781.00 (base bid including
contingency). At the March 3, 2026, City Council meeting, City Council approved the bid add
alternate #1 totaling $112,672.40.

It has since been identified that the Council of Michigan Foundations approved on May 7, 2026,
the reallocation of funds for tree removal to fence installation required for the courts. The trees are
no longer required for removal because they were deemed healthy and do not obstruct the Ewalt
Center demolition or court improvement project.

The funding source is as follows:


    •   Bid Alternate #4 total $50,700.00 (Fence Installation)

           o   $27,289.00 - 101-818-818.000-SPARKG- Other Professional Services

           o   $23,411.00- 101-818-816.000-Contracted Construction Services

With the reallocation of $27,289.00 in grant funds awarded and $23,411.00 from the general fund,
the total project amount will increase to the not-to-exceed amount of $459,153.40



Funding & Contingency
Funding for the Galloway Lake Park Court Improvements Project is available through the Council
of Michigan Foundations (CMF) and Michigan Department of Natural Resources (DNR) SPARK
Grant Program. As part of this contract modification, the project scope is being revised to remove
the tree and brush-clearing component previously budgeted at $27,289.00 and reallocate those
funds to Bid Alternate #4, which provides fencing improvements for the new pickleball courts. Bid
Alternate #4 has a total cost of $50,700.00. Of this amount, $27,289.00 will be funded through the
reallocated project funds originally designated for tree and brush removal. The remaining
$23,411.00 will be funded through the City's General Fund. With the inclusion of Bid Alternate #1
and Bid Alternate #4, the revised total contract amount for the project shall not exceed
$459,153.40. Adequate grant and City funding have been identified and are available to support
the revised project scope.


Recommendation

Parks and Recreation staff recommend that the City Council approve the revised project scope and
authorize the award to WCI Contractors in an amount not to exceed $459,153.40, inclusive of Bid
Alternate #1 and Bid Alternate #4.

Approval of this resolution will allow the City to enhance the project by installing fencing around
the pickleball courts while utilizing existing project funds previously allocated for tree and brush
removal and providing the remaining balance through the General Fund. Staff believe these
improvements will better support the long-term functionality, safety, and user experience of the
facility and recommend City Council approval.


                          CITY OF PONTIAC CITY COUNCIL
 Resolution to Approve Change Order Increasing Not-to-Exceed Amount for
        Galloway Lake Park Court Improvements (Bid Alternate #4)


WHEREAS, at its meeting held on February 17, 2026, the Pontiac City Council approved a
contract with WCI Contractors for the Galloway Lake Park Court Improvement Project in the
amount of $295,781.00; and,

WHEREAS, at its meeting held on March 3, 2026, the Pontiac City Council approved Bid
Alternate #1 in the amount of $112,672.40, increasing the total authorized contract amount to
$408,453.40; and,

WHEREAS, the Council of Michigan Foundations (CMF) approved a modification to the SPARK
Grant project scope on May 7, 2026, allowing funds previously allocated for tree and brush
removal to be reallocated toward fencing installation associated with the pickleball courts; and,

WHEREAS, the trees originally identified for removal have since been determined to be healthy
and do not interfere with either the Ewalt Center demolition project or the Galloway Lake Park
Court Improvements Project; and,

WHEREAS, Bid Alternate #4 provides for the installation of fencing at a cost of $50,700.00; and,

WHEREAS, funding for Bid Alternate #4 shall be provided as follows:

    •   $27,289.00 from GL Account No. 101-818-818.000-SPARKG - Other Professional
        Services, utilizing grant funds previously allocated for tree and brush removal; and

    •   $23,411.00 from GL Account No. 101-818-816.000 - Contracted Construction Services;
        and,

WHEREAS, approval of Bid Alternate #4 will increase the total authorized contract amount by
$50,700.00, resulting in a revised not-to-exceed contract amount of $459,153.40; and,

WHEREAS, the City Council finds that the installation of fencing around the pickleball courts is
in the best interest of the City and will enhance the safety, functionality, and long-term usability of
the facility; now,


THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Pontiac City Council hereby approves the revised
project scope for the Galloway Lake Park Court Improvements Project and authorizes the inclusion
of Bid Alternate #4 for fence installation; and further

RESOLVED that the City Council approves a change order increasing the contract with WCI
Contractors by $50,700.00 and authorizes a revised total contract amount not to exceed Four
Hundred Fifty-Nine Thousand One Hundred Fifty-Three Dollars and Forty Cents ($459,153.40),
inclusive of the base bid, Bid Alternate #1, and Bid Alternate #4; and further

RESOLVED, that the Mayor or his designee and the City Clerk are authorized to execute all
documents necessary to implement this resolution, and that City administration is authorized to
take all actions necessary to carry out the intent of this resolution.

                        CITY OF PONTIAC CITY COUNCIL

RESOLUTION EXTENDING THE TEMPORARY MORATORIUM ON THE
  ESTABLISHMENT, PERMITTING, CONSIDERATION, APPROVAL,
CONSTRUCTION AND/OR INSTALLATION OF DATA CENTERS WITHIN
                  THE CITY OF PONTIAC

WHEREAS, on January 20, 2026, the City Council adopted a resolution imposing a temporary
. six (6) month moratorium on the establishment, permitting, consideration, approval, construction
and/or installation of data centers within the City of Pontiac; and,

WHEREAS, the temporary moratorium is set to expire on July 20, 2026; and,

WHEREAS, the City Council finds that additional time is necessary to complete review and
consideration of potential zoning ordinance amendments or other regulations addressing data
centers; and,

WHEREAS, the City Council desires to extend the temporary moratorium for one additional six
(6) month period, but does not intend to authorize any further extensions of the moratorium; now,

THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the City Council of the City of Pontiac hereby extends
the temporary moratorium on the establishment, permitting, consideration, approval, construction
and/or installation of data centers within the City of Pontiac for an additional six (6) months
following July 20, 2026; and further

RESOLVED that the moratorium shall expire on January 20, 2027, unless earlier terminated by
the City Council, and shall automatically terminate upon the effective date of any zoning ordinance
amendment adopted by the City Council regulating data centers within the City; and further

RESOLVED that no further extensions of the moratorium are authorized; and further

RESOLVED that, except as expressly modified by this Resolution, all terms and provisions of the
original moratorium resolution remain in full force and effect.

Overview
Gun violence continues to impact public safety in Pontiac, particularly in high-density residential
areas. The City of Pontiac has invested resources and undertaken myriad strategies and initiatives to
prevent violent crime. The current and previous City Administration and City Council has
established and expanded the Pontiac SAFE violence intervention initiatives and invested in
expanded capacity and responsiveness with our Oakland County Sheriff Department contract.
The City of Pontiac recognizes gun violence as a major contributor to negative health outcomes, as
well as a negative impact on the quality of life for our residents, and City Council has recently
adopted a Resolution identified gun violence as a public health epidemic in our community.
The rates of incidents of violent crime continue to decrease in the City of Pontiac, but we are
committed to further preventing future incidents and further decreasing those rates. The Newman
Lane, Spring Lake, and North Hill Farms apartment complexes have experienced elevated levels of


gun-related incidents. Traditional 911 reporting does not capture all gunfire activity, resulting in
gaps in response and enforcement.
Raven Gunshot Detection Technology provides real-time, location-based alerts that enable faster
and more accurate law enforcement response. The system is now operated under the Flock Safety
platform (Flock Group Inc.). The previous Administration authorized a six-month pilot program
undertaken in collaboration with the Oakland County Sheriff Department, whereby the Raven
Gunshot Detection Technology would be utilized within the City of Pontiac to improve crime
prevention and crime incident responsiveness and assess the efficacy of the technology for our city's
needs. According to the Raven analytics report (May 8, 2026), the system generated 736 total alerts
during the deployment period, including 269 gunshot-related alerts, 212 fireworks alerts, and 19
sideshow alerts.
Raven technology has directly supported 11 significant criminal investigations, including 2 homicide
cases both solved in large part with Raven-generated evidence, 4 attempted murder cases, and 3
felons in possession of a firearm case.



Recommendation
The Mayor's Office recommends adoption of this Resolution, which would authorize the continued
deployment, operation, and utilization of the Raven Gunshot Detection system within Newman
Lane, Spring Lake, and North Hill Farms apartment communities in coordination with the Oakland
County Sheriffs Office. We are committed to further improving the safety of our Pontiac
neighborhoods and further decreasing our violent crime rates, and we believe that this is an
appropriate and effective technology to help accomplish those goals.


                         CITY OF PONTIAC CITY COUNCIL

 RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING CONTINUED UTILIZATION OF RAVEN
  GUNSHOT DETECTION TECHNOLOGY IN THE CITY OF PONTIAC

WHEREAS, the City of Pontiac is committed to ensuring the safety and well-being of all residents,
businesses, and visitors; and,
WHEREAS, gun violence continues to pose a significant threat to public safety and quality of life
within the City of Pontiac, particularly in certain high-density residential areas; and,
WHEREAS, the Newman Lane, Spring Lake, and North Hill Farms apartment communities have
been identified as locations experiencing a disproportionate volume of criminal activity, including
gun-related incidents; and,
WHEREAS, rapid and accurate detection of gunfire incidents can significantly improve emergency
response times, assist law enforcement investigations, and enhance community safety outcomes
within the City of Pontiac; and,
WHEREAS, Raven Gunshot Detection Technology is an advanced, real-time system operated
through the Flock Safety platform (Flock Group Inc.) that detects, locates, and alerts law
enforcement to suspected gunfire incidents using acoustic sensors and data analysis; and,
WHEREAS, the Raven analytics report dated May 8, 2026, reflects the following activity within
the deployment period: a total of736 alerts were generated including 269 gunshot-related alerts, 212
fireworks alerts, and 19 sideshow alerts; and,
WHEREAS, Raven technology has directly assisted law enforcement in 11 major criminal
incidents, including 2 homicide investigations both solved in large part through evidence collected
by the Raven Gunshot Detection system, 4 attempted murder cases, and 3 felons in possession of a
firearm cases; and,
WHEREAS, the Oakland County Sheriffs Office holds the vendor contract with Flock Group Inc.
for this technology, and the City of Pontiac's continued participation requires formal City Council
authorization; and,
WHEREAS, the annual cost for continued deployment is $36,000.00, covering designated areas,
with a 24-month contract total of $72,000.00; and,
WHEREAS, the pilot period for this technology has concluded-and the City of Pontiac seeks to
continue and maintain the Raven Gunshot Detection system within the identified communities to
support law enforcement response and enhance public safety; now,


THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Pontiac City Council hereby authorizes the continued
deployment, operation, and utilization of the Raven Gunshot Detection system within the Newman
Lane, Spring Lake, and North Hill Farms apartment communities, in coordination with the Oakland
County Sheriffs Office, in an annual amount not to exceed $36,000.00; and further
RESOLVED, that the Mayor or his designee is authorized and directed to execute any agreements
or documents necessary to implement the continued deployment of the Raven Gunshot Detection
system on behalf of the City of Pontiac, subject to approval as to form by the City Attorney; and
further
RESOLVED, that the City Clerk is authorized and directed to transmit copies of this resolution to
the Oakland County Sheriffs Office and other relevant stakeholders.
